text:
Here’s how we’ll make this COI valuable. Every session will be engaging, practical, and something you actually look forward to.

We’ll keep you updated, bring in relevant speakers, and give you space to learn and contribute.

name: TextBox 6
text:
Knowledge-crib
Version-controlled context for software agents
Index once. Serve precise code relationships over MCP. Help agents discover architecture, trace change impact, and work with far less raw context.
v0.1.0 Release Candidate | Apache-2.0 | Local-first deterministic core | Optional grounded LLM enrichment
Created & architected by Vishal Chawla
textPreview: Knowledge-crib | Version-controlled context for software agents | Index once. Serve precise code relationships over MCP. Help agents disc...

text: Knowledge-crib is version-controlled context infrastructure for software agents. It indexes a repository into a portable project soul, then serves precise code relationships through MCP. Core path is deterministic, local-first, and zero-network. Optional LLM enrichment remains separately grounded. I created and architected this release candidate and propose validating it through a controlled pilot.

name: TextBox 4
text: Every session rereads code to recover context already learned. Cost repeats across developers and agents.
textPreview: Every session rereads code to recover context already learned. Cost repeats across developers and agents.

name: TextBox 7
text: Large raw context adds file reads, tokens, and turnaround time before useful work begins.
textPreview: Large raw context adds file reads, tokens, and turnaround time before useful work begins.

name: TextBox 11
text: File-level views miss callers, contracts, and cross-service impact — creating review load and regressions.
textPreview: File-level views miss callers, contracts, and cross-service impact — creating review load and regressions.

name: TextBox 12
text: Root cause: context stays temporary and unstructured. Knowledge-crib turns repository structure into durable, queryable memory.
textPreview: Root cause: context stays temporary and unstructured. Knowledge-crib turns repository structure into durable, queryable memory.

text: AI coding agents repeatedly rebuild context. That creates repeated discovery cost, slower decisions, and unsafe changes when callers or cross-service contracts remain unseen. Knowledge-crib converts temporary file-reading context into durable, queryable repository memory.

name: Table 18
preview: Cross-package task | Without crib | With crib

text: Two reproducible workloads show current measured value. Cross-package task drops from 26,286 to 1,415 context tokens: 18.58 times fewer. Across six graph-wide discovery queries, default crib responses use 3,339 tokens versus 151,072 raw-file tokens: 45.24 times leaner. Scripts and pricing inputs ship in repository, and CI requires at least three-times saving.

Pilot remains controlled because release candidate still needs large-enterprise scale proof, centralized access controls, and extractor-specific fidelity assessment. Two-week rollout measures before standardizing.
